items.quote: This woman said to me, ‘Give up your son so we may eat him today, and tomorrow we’ll eat my son.’
items.contrast: The first woman’s son is to be eaten today, while the quoted woman’s own son is to be eaten tomorrow.
items.reason: The key follows the quoted woman’s proposal. However, “the other woman” is an avoidably vague label because the question does not explicitly establish which woman is the reference point.

items.quote: Zechariah, who instructed him in the fear of God.
items.contrast: Zechariah instructed Uzziah, whereas Amaziah is identified as the father whose good conduct Uzziah followed.
items.reason: The relative clause directly identifies Zechariah as Uzziah’s instructor, distinguishing that role from Amaziah’s role as his father and example.

items.quote: came to Jehoiada the priest. Then he gave the commanders the spears and shields
items.contrast: Jehoiada gives the weapons to the commanders; David is only their former owner.
items.reason: The antecedent of “he” is Jehoiada. The passage separately says that the weapons had belonged to King David, which does not make David the giver in this event.

items.quote: the king had put the officer on whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate, and the people trampled him in the gateway
items.contrast: The officer is trampled, while the king is the person who had appointed him to oversee the gate.
items.reason: The pronoun “him” refers to the officer introduced immediately before it, not to the king.

items.quote: I solemnly consecrate my silver to the Lord for my son to make an image overlaid with silver.
items.contrast: The mother says that her son will make the image, although the later action says that a silversmith actually makes it.
items.reason: The question asks specifically about the mother’s statement, so her son is the unique answer; this requires distinguishing her stated plan from the subsequent event.
